titulo: Scroll that controls time: the cARCKHÉtic scroll skill
lead: The engine that ties scrolling to frames has few parts, and each one fixes a measured stutter. You look at the parts, swap the kit page's frames for your own from lesson 2, prove with the test contract that the right frame shows up at each point, and ask the scroll-film-studio skill, from ARCKHÉ, for the new page.
objetivo: tie your frames to the kit's scroll engine, prove it with the ?jump and __ready contract, and ask the skill for the page.

aprende.t: The engine parts: track, progress, smoothed playhead, bitmap window
The test contract ?jump=[y] + window.__ready, and why without it there is no verification
Install the scroll-film-studio skill and ask for the page through Lane A, with no generator
The copy gate: the page sells, it doesn't narrate the camera

hero_alt: Mouse with a scroll wheel in focus on a dark desk, with a monitor in the background showing a page with a lens.

secoes.sub: The parts of motor-rolagem.js (site-movimento, ARCKHÉ). Click each one.

nos.detalhe: A 400vh section (four screens) with a stage pinned to the top (position: sticky). While the track scrolls past, the stage stays put and the canvas swaps frames.
progress = −track top ÷ (track height − screen height), clamped between 0 and 1. Target frame = progress × (frames − 1).
On each browser frame, the current frame moves 14% of the way toward the target (lerp 0.14). Tying it straight to the target feels mechanical; with smoothing the film glides.

Drawing a JPEG that hasn't been decoded yet stalls the page. The engine decodes off the main thread (createImageBitmap) the frames 2 s ahead and 1.4 s behind, and drops the rest. The window is measured in seconds of film, not in frames.
Download one frame in every 8 first: any point in the scroll already has a nearby frame to show, never a black screen. Then the rest, at most 10 at a time. A frame missing? Draw the closest one.
It covers the screen while the crop is small (up to 22% of the frame); past that, it fits the whole frame with bands. Density 1 (dpr: 1): the 1024 px frame drawn 1:1, with no scaling up.

secoes.legenda: In site-movimento, the bitmap window fix took the worst scroll hitch from 150–315 ms down to 33–36 ms (README and engine comment, 10/18/2026).

secoes.sub: Two lines that both ARCKHÉ skills require on every page they build.

texto: The page reads the jump parameter from the URL and scrolls to y pixels before anything else, with no smooth scrolling. Opening the page at 50% becomes a URL.
The kit's engine does this in MotionEngine.ready.
After positioning and drawing, the page sets window.__ready = true. The test waits for that flag instead of waiting a fixed time.
Waiting 2 s "to be safe" passes on your machine and fails on a loaded one.
Screenshot, verifier, and the agent checking its own work, all through the same path.
The skill's verify.js refuses to capture the screen if __ready never arrives.

secoes.sub: ARCKHÉ skill for Codex and Claude Code: interview, concepts, art direction, page, and gates. Two lanes: Lane A code only (no cost) and Lane B with film from your generator. The kit's verificar.mjs reads the kit's hooks ([data-filme] section, #tela canvas, window.__filme, and window.__filmeInfo) in addition to the contract; that's why the prompt tells the skill to start from kit/site. A page built from scratch by the skill checks out with its own verify.js.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: Scrolling stutters the first time you scroll fast. Which part of the engine fixes this?
opcoes: Preload all the frames before showing the page.
Replace the canvas with a video.
The bitmap window: decode the frames near the playhead ahead of time.
perguntas.explica: The stutter is JPEG decoding at draw time. The window decodes ahead, off the main thread. Preloading everything is heavy and does not avoid decoding; density 2 doubles the work.

perguntas.p: Why does the checker wait for window.__ready instead of waiting 2 seconds?
opcoes: Because 2 s is too short for Chromium to open.
Because the page knows when it has finished positioning and drawing; a fixed time passes on one machine and fails on another.
Because GitHub Pages blocks fixed waits.
perguntas.explica: A fixed time is a guess: on a loaded machine the drawing is late and the test reads a black screen. The __ready flag says exactly when to look.

perguntas.p: Which of these sentences does the copy gate reject for a lens film?
opcoes: "The camera moves through the glass to the aperture."
"Made for scenes that happen in low light."
"780 g, fits on a handheld stabilizer."
perguntas.explica: Narrating the camera is shooting script, not copy for a buyer. The person is already watching the film; the text says what the image does not.

perguntas.p: In the scroll-film-studio skill, what changes between Lane A and Lane B?
opcoes: Lane A is made for a phone held upright and Lane B for a computer screen.
Lane B does not need frames.
Lane A is code only; Lane B uses clips from your generator.
Lane A uses Three.js and B uses 2D canvas.
perguntas.explica: Lane A: motion in code, zero cost. Lane B: a film generated as chained clips, with the bill and credits of your generator.

itens.texto: Track, progress, smoothed playhead, bitmap window, 1 in 8 load.
?jump=[y] positions, window.__ready signals: without it there is no test.
scroll-film-studio through Lane A, with a copy gate.
